messages.content: Write a polished 400-to-500-word contemporary American English scene between two adult coworkers who have become close friends. They are finishing a routine task near the end of the workday. Let workplace details ground the scene, but make the relationship feel personal rather than office-comedy caricature. Include mild humor, a practical disagreement, and one quieter moment.

The office was mostly empty by six, but the printer near the reception desk was still running.

“That's the third copy.”

Alex looked at the pages coming out. “I know.”

“Then why are you printing it again?”

“Because the margins are wrong.”

Jordan picked up the first stack from the tray.

“They look fine.”

“You say that about everything.”

“I have low standards.”

“You have a high tolerance for ugly documents.”

Jordan smiled. “That's probably why we're friends.”

Alex took the pages from her.

“We're friends because you keep bringing snacks.”

“That too.”

The printer stopped.

Alex looked at the screen.

“Finally.”

Jordan glanced at the clock.

“Do you need to stay?”

“No.”

“Then let's go.”

Alex stacked the papers neatly.

“I want to finish this first.”

“You've said that for twenty minutes.”

“It's almost done.”

Jordan leaned against the desk.

“You know nobody is going to remember whether page four had the same margin as page five.”

“I will.”

“Exactly.”

Alex looked at her.

“What?”

“Nothing.”

“That was a look.”

Jordan shrugged.

“You're doing that thing again.”

“What thing?”

“Trying to fix everything because it's easier than admitting you're tired.”

Alex stared at the paper in her hand.

“You've known me too long.”

“Unfortunately.”

Alex laughed quietly.

She set the pages down.

“Okay.”

Jordan picked up her bag.

“Okay what?”

“I'm done.”

“Great.”

They started toward the elevator.

Alex stopped.

“What?” Jordan asked.

“I forgot the lights.”

Jordan sighed.

“Of course you did.”

Alex went back toward the office.

Jordan followed.

“You know, one day I'm going to stop following you.”

“No, you won't.”

“How confident.”

“You've been saying it for two years.”

Jordan reached the door and held it open.

“That's because you keep proving me right.”

Alex shut off the lights.

The hallway went dim except for the emergency signs.

Jordan waited beside the elevator.

“You okay?” she asked.

Alex nodded.

“Yeah.”

A beat passed.

“Thanks for staying.”

Jordan pressed the elevator button.

“Yeah.”

The doors opened.

“Tomorrow,” Alex said.

“Tomorrow.”
